sources.entry: agent-qa — Self-improving agentic QA harness with memory for natural-language web and mobile test execution.
agent-qa - Self-improving QA agent for web and mobile apps with natural-language tests, run memory, and regression detection. #testing #free

summary.one_liner: agent-qa is a self-improving QA harness that runs natural-language test journeys on web, Android and iOS apps, keeping run evidence and a reviewable memory of facts and procedures.
summary.what_it_does: Takes a user journey described in plain language and executes it against web, Android, or iOS targets, saving evidence from each run. It can be driven from a CLI, a dashboard, or a coding agent through MCP and skills. Its "memidex" component stores facts and working procedures as reviewable files inside the user's repository. The README says the system validates lessons from runs, retires stale knowledge, and uses user feedback to correct mistakes. Failed steps are shown with their screenshots, and a run can be inspected to see which memory it used. The README also cites benchmark results on AndroidWorld and AppControlBench, which are described on the project blog rather than in the README itself.
use_cases: automated end-to-end testing of web apps from plain-language descriptions
mobile app testing on Android and iOS
regression testing of user journeys like checkout
QA with an AI coding agent via MCP
reviewing screenshots and evidence of failed test steps
keeping AI test knowledge in the repository
how_to_run: Connect a model and run the demo by following the quickstart (linked from the README)
notable: Memory stored as reviewable files in the repository (memidex)
Self-improvement: validates lessons from runs and retires stale knowledge
Failed steps shown alongside screenshots, with memory traceability
Works through CLI, dashboard, or coding agent via MCP and skills
caveats: README says early stage and expects bugs
Requires connecting a model to run tests
keywords: test my app in plain english
share test knowledge with my team
